note: An application, not a library, selected against criteria frozen before any candidate was examined and without regard to Understanding's performance against it. One row per encoder version, append-only. Read the IR-7 row's note before comparing its opacity with the other corpora.

rows.note: First measurement. 37.1% opaque is NOT comparable to toml-python's 13.6% without this note: 126 of the 209 opaque statements are docstrings, which are expression statements containing a bare string and carry no semantics at all. Excluding them the rate is 83 of 437 = 19.0%, which is the figure comparable to the other corpora. Counting docstrings as unrepresented semantics is a defect in the instrument, recorded here and not fixed in this round because the encoder was frozen through corpus selection.

IR-9 classifies every statement as semantic, non-semantic or metadata, and only an unrepresented SEMANTIC statement counts as opaque. The statement count changed legitimately because 126 non-semantic and 2 metadata statements left the denominator: they carry no execution semantics and were previously counted as unrepresented semantics. Intrinsic fingerprints changed wherever a function body contained a docstring or a bare string statement, which was expected and not predicted stable. Nothing else changed: no new resolution, no import modelling, no loop or exception representation.

C-2 split Python's `yield` into value-stream-emission (a generator hands a value to a consumer) and scoped-resource-handoff (a @contextmanager hands a resource to the caller's scope). The 23 statements that were `other` are the same 23 statements, renamed: 20 emission and 3 handoff, at cli/tools.py 40 and 220 and cli/__init__.py 433. Nothing is represented that was not represented before, so 435 semantic statements, 81 opaque, 126 non-semantic and 2 metadata statements left the denominator exactly as at IR-9. One collision fingerprint moved, 755edd5db3a2ff2ef7e27bc to 937136f1518166f9c151c29c, which is the _open pair whose yields were reclassified; the other seven are unchanged. The handoff classification rests on the decorator's name, which is DECLARED_BY_AUTHOR knowledge and not a fact derived from program semantics; aliases, imported renames, wrappers, and hand-written context managers are not recognised.

C-3 moved Python's `with` from exception-handling to scoped-resource: a scope that acquires a resource, runs under its lifetime, and releases it on every exit. Releasing on an exception is a consequence of that lifetime, not the purpose of the construct. exception-handling 17 to 10, all seven of the difference being `with` statements; `try` is untouched. The same 81 statements are opaque and the same 435 are semantic; 126 non-semantic and 2 metadata statements left the denominator exactly as at IR-9. One collision fingerprint moved, 937136f1518166f9c151c29c to 2fe3b1a0f4f1dfcd9266565d, the _open pair, which holds both a reclassified `with` and the handoff yields C-2 renamed; the other seven are unchanged. Classification only: acquisition, release ordering, and failure propagation are all still unrepresented.

C-4 moved a nested def from declaration to local-function-construction: execution constructs a function value and binds it within an enclosing executable scope. declaration 6 to 0, local-function-construction 6, at cli/harvest.py 140, cli/tools.py 117, 123 and 297, raw.py 151, and visitors.py 383. The category is deliberately NOT closure construction: an inspection of all six found that only three capture an enclosing binding, so a closure claim would have been false for half of them. All eight collision fingerprints are unchanged, because none of the six sits in a function that collides with another. 435 semantic statements, 81 opaque, 126 non-semantic and 2 metadata statements left the denominator, exactly as at IR-9.

C-5 changed the Python adapter's handling of a bare await statement (an awaited call stays a represented call effect; an awaited non-call becomes completion-dependency), and this corpus contains no bare await, so every measured value is identical to the C-4 row. The adapter's version moved because its behaviour moved, not because this corpus exercises it; the behaviour is proved by fixture. 435 semantic statements, 81 opaque, 126 non-semantic and 2 metadata statements left the denominator.

R-1A, ir_schema 6: the IR gained the `awaited` expression modifier and the `evaluate` carrier. This corpus contains no await, so every category, count and collision-group MEMBERSHIP is identical to the C-5 row. Every fingerprint VALUE changed because the schema number is hashed into the fingerprint; that is a property of the fingerprint, not a change in any function's semantics, and the frozen prediction that only await-bearing functions would move was wrong for that reason (see the log). 126 non-semantic and 2 metadata statements left the denominator.
